name: Directed Overpressure Charge
description:
The DOC-7 is a shaped-charge demolition device engineered to produce a unidirectional pressure wave rather than an omnidirectional blast. Unlike conventional explosives that waste energy in all directions simultaneously, the DOC-7 uses a parabolic copper-composite reflector plate cast directly into the charge body. On detonation, the reflector focuses approximately 78% of the blast energy into a forward cone of roughly 40 degrees, producing an overpressure front capable of collapsing reinforced concrete walls, shearing door mechanisms, and incapacitating personnel in the target corridor without destroying the structure behind the operator.

The charge uses a linear magnetic acceleration trigger system: a small magnetic initiator rail drives a tungsten striker into the primary detonator at precisely calibrated velocity, ensuring consistent detonation timing regardless of ambient temperature or humidity — a common failure point in legacy explosive initiators used in GLMZ's variable-climate sublevels. This consistency makes the DOC-7 reliable in flooded infrastructure, high-EMF environments, and extreme cold, all common conditions in the city's lower tiers.

PALLADIAN CONSTRUCTION originally developed the DOC-7 for controlled demolition of condemned hab-blocks, where precision was necessary to avoid collapsing adjacent structures. The design was licensed to ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS, who militarized it with a magnetic initiator rail and reduced the charge mass for operator carry. The civilian and military versions are nearly identical in external appearance, a fact that has created significant legal ambiguity in GLMZ's courts.
specifications:
weight: 1.2kg
dimensions: 180mm x 90mm x 70mm
blast cone: 40-degree forward arc
effective range: Up to 12m in target cone
blast energy focus: 78% forward, 22% lateral/rear
initiator: Magnetic rail-driven tungsten striker
back blast zone: 2m — operator must not stand directly behind
wall penetration: Up to 220mm reinforced concrete
tactical_use: Standard use is magnetic attachment to a door, wall, or bulkhead, followed by operator withdrawal to the side — never behind — before remote or timed detonation. The directional blast breaches the target structure and incapacitates anyone within the forward cone, while the operator position avoids the back-blast. In military use, DOC-7s are stacked in sequence for breach-and-clear operations through multiple walls. Some operators use them defensively, mounting them on tripwires to channelize enemy movement into the blast cone.
cultural_context: In GLMZ's construction and demolition industry, DOC-7s are familiar tools — licensed contractors carry them routinely for teardown work in the condemned mid-tier hab districts. This normalizes their presence in ways that make them difficult to police. The military variant is distinguished by its matte-black housing versus the civilian orange, but both can be operated identically. Criminal organizations favor them for vault breaching. The phrase 'sending the push' has entered street slang as a term for delivering an ultimatum that cannot be refused.
known_users: Vault thieves and corporate espionage operators
story_hooks: A series of fatal 'demolition accidents' in the mid-tier hab district all involve DOC-7 detonations — but the buildings weren't condemned, and the victims weren't workers.

A player needs to breach a corporate vault and acquires a DOC-7 through a construction contact — only to discover the device is the military variant, recently stolen, and ARCTURUS is actively tracking it.
PALLADIAN CONSTRUCTION's civilian DOC-7 licensing database has been hacked and all records deleted. Someone is making legitimate-looking units disappear off the books.
